newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia plans new air links to Asia regions.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia plans new air links to Asia regions.

text.p: Australia plans to link the northern part of the country to its near neighbours in the Asia Pacific region with new aviation services, Australian transport minister John Sharp said on Friday.
"Australia is pursuing the development of regional airlinks between north Australia and other countries to its near north," Sharp said in a speech to the aviation press club.

Sharp said it would link its northernmost city Darwin in the Northern Territory with regional centres in Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Brunei and Papua New Guinea. He said the plan would exclude the major cities in each of the countries.
"The objective being to build regional links that are attractive to airlines, niche operators and or tourism investors," Sharp said.
Sharp said Australian regional airline National Jet Systems had already started services between Darwin and Indonesia.

"I think there will be other Australian operators to take up the opportunity to provide a regional airline service across national borders from points in northern Australia, whether it be with Indonesia, but also in Paupa New Guinea, Philippines, Brunei and Malaysia and so we see great opportunity there."
Sharp said the agreement with Indonesia followed the pact struck last week between Australian and its northern neighbour to expand economic cooperation to develop the archipelago's eastern islands.
The economic pact to establish a sub-regional economic pact called the Australia-Indonesia Development Area (AIDA).
"We are keen to particpate in that, there would be a great opportunity for Australia," Sharp said in reference to AIDA.
"In a course in a country like Indonesia that has 17,000 islands, air services are important for economic development."
Sharp said talks were continuing on specific areas in Indonesia that the aviation agreement would cover.

The agreements between Australia and its neighbours allowed for regional airline services as opposed to international services and would be similar to the aviation services that are provided between regional areas in Australia, Sharp said.
Sharp said the government would also negotiate arrangements with Indonesia on fast-ferry services to Indonesia from Darwin.
The minister said further talks on the agreement between Australia and Indonesia would be held in Darwin on November 14.
Over the past two weeks Australia has set up plans for new route arrangements between Darwin and the southern Philippines and between northern Australia and Papua New Guinea.
Sharp said the government would continue to raise with its bilateral partners the questions of developing routes and special arrangements.
